brief: Core CPI rose 0.33% month-over-month in September, above Goldman Sachs's 0.24% estimate and the 0.2% median forecast. The surprise was led by shelter: OER rose 0.35% month-over-month, contributing 12bp to core, about 5bp more than GS expected, with the strength concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, seasonally adjusted by GS) while the Northeast, West and South matched GS's trend estimate. Travel services (lodging +2.0%, airfares +1.2%, 6bp), autos (3bp, matching GS's expected pickup), and recreation (toys and games +4.2%, a volatile category, 3bp) also ran firm. Headline CPI rose 0.65% month-over-month, close to GS's and the median's forecasts, on energy prices up 5.2% tied to the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran. Both CPI and core CPI accelerated year-over-year versus the prior month and came in above GS and consensus. From the report's details, GS raised its September core PCE estimate to 0.32% (from a pre-release 0.20%), a 3.09% year-over-year pace, on the same OER, hotels and recreation upside, and now expects headline PCE rose 0.49% month-over-month, 3.62% year-over-year. GS says the report raises the odds of an October hike but still expects the Fed's second hike in December, pending tomorrow's PPI report and Chairman Warsh's IMF speech in Bangkok.
